name: Agent reliability, boundaries and operational accountability
observation: Real-world agent boundary errors and new payment/identity tooling both increase the importance of scoped access, traceability and fail-safe controls.
strongest_support: Reuters Sep 4 reported German wiki agent incident; Circle's official agent wallet announcements document market direction.
counterevidence: Some episodes cite uncontrolled 400-agent or penetration-testing anecdotes. Platform products have unknown user adoption and may be unnecessary for small workflows.
first_test: Add an agent run ledger, spend cap, tool allowlist, approvals and test fixtures to one existing workflow; compare incident diagnosis and recovery time.

name: Model claims versus real-world performance
observation: Measured company revenue, simulated silicon performance, benchmark adapter scores and apparently proved math problems represent fundamentally different kinds of evidence.
strongest_support: NVIDIA financial release verifies actual revenue; Architect Labs labels efficiency number a projection; ARC Prize harness differences and Clay proof-review stages document evaluation dependencies.
counterevidence: Peer-reviewed or accredited independent replications are still missing for important project claims, and model benchmarks may be optimized against test methodology.
first_test: Publish an evidence-stage table for each technology: claim, test hardware/software, original metric, comparator, methodology, independent reviewer and date.

name: Practical small-business AI offerings
observation: Product-market evidence and proof of completed work matter more than generic AI capabilities. Prize finalists selected from 26,000 registrants are not a base rate.
strongest_support: XPRIZE lists Polyfork revenue and paying customer count, plus Mexico VAT workflow finalist; X's own operating manual describes rapid economic kill tests.
counterevidence: Organizers' figures are not independently audited profit/retention; no assurance comparable developer businesses will win customers; health and financial workflows have legal scope constraints.
first_test: Choose one tedious, authorized business workflow, prove measurable savings or error reduction on real examples and request a paid pilot, without building a platform.

name: AI science, medicine and validation stages
observation: Novel research and approved clinical products are not equivalent. Mathematical apparent proofs await scrutiny; biologic discoveries need experimental validation; clinical trial authorization precedes marketing approval.
strongest_support: Clay Sept 11 proof evaluation; United Therapeutics SEC filings on investigational xenotransplant programs; Nature semi-autonomous lab work and Merck's oncology trial announcements.
counterevidence: Some striking clinical statistics are early trial endpoints or sponsor reports; scientific reproducibility and regulatory endpoint requirements may change timelines.
first_test: Track official clinical trial identifiers, trial phase, endpoint, peer-review, agency decision and comparable baseline separately; make no medical recommendation from a podcast.

name: AI compute, energy and national competition
observation: Energy availability, chip access, product pricing, and physical infrastructure all limit scaling; a single US–China AGI race metric obscures these bottlenecks.
strongest_support: Duke's modeled grid-load flexibility, IEA's current sodium-ion scale, Stanford AI Index capability comparisons, official NVIDIA quarterly revenue.
counterevidence: Infrastructure build-out assumptions often conflate capacity with actual deployment; rapid changes in government export rules alter comparisons.
first_test: When choosing model vendors for a client, benchmark total effective cost, availability, privacy regime and reliability of a non-sensitive representative workflow.

name: Robotics and physical autonomy
observation: Prize demonstrations, single-task speed demonstrations, robotaxi fleet safety statistics and humanoid forecasts have different deployment readiness.
strongest_support: Official XPRIZE Wildfire contest awards, Waymo public service and safety metrics, ARK's own robotics expectations.
counterevidence: Operators and investors have commercial incentives, and standardized independent real-world humanoid reliability evaluations remain limited.
first_test: Define operational safety, task-completion and human intervention rates for a named robotics application instead of extrapolating from video highlights.

name: Creative futures and media contests
observation: AI-assisted creation lowers some entry barriers; optimistic creative works can attract prize and financing attention, but production investment is not identical to cash prizes or market traction.
strongest_support: Google and XPRIZE independently describe announced winners and funding types.
counterevidence: Claims that upbeat fiction alone makes frontier models safer are not established causally; selection bias in prizes is very strong.
first_test: Produce a single commissioned, rights-cleared story/trailer with user feedback and a human editorial review; do not infer general commercial demand from contest winnings.
